brief.headline: Reported revenue of $81.61B for the quarter ended 2026-04-26 is the highest of 63 reported periods, with networking carrying 21.5% of the annual revenue change at 10.0% of the base, R&D falling to 8.6% of revenues from 9.9%, and two of three tested 'record' statements holding only within the same fiscal quarter.

threads.title: Growth and where it came from
threads.reading: The financial condition check found nothing crossing a threshold, so the concern the checks raise is composition rather than condition. Networking grew from $12.99B to $31.38B, an $18.39B increase carrying 21.5% of the total revenue movement while standing at 10.0% of the prior-period base — 2.2x its weight (Revenue composition, Class A, 10-K filed 2026-02-25). The claims check confirmed $81.61B for the quarter ended 2026-04-26 as the highest of 63 prior reported periods, but marked two statements from the same release as records only within the same fiscal quarter, a 17-period comparison set.
supporting: 'Record revenue of $81.6 billion, up 85% from a year ago' tested SUPPORTED — the highest of 63 prior reported periods, against a prior best of $57.01B for 2025-10-26 (Management claims check, Class B release measured against Class A figures).
The financial condition check found nothing crossing a threshold, and the single-source supply language check flagged nothing either (Class A).
The restatement check surfaced only two revisions, both to fiscal 2016 quarters and both filed 2018-02-28; 484 reported figures are on file with 0 new to the ledger (Class A, SEC XBRL company facts).
against: Networking at 10.0% of revenue carried 21.5% of the total revenue change — 2.2x its weight, the only composition finding flagged (Revenue composition check, Class A, segment revenue schedule).

Two of three tested statements came back QUALIFIED: a record only within the same fiscal quarter, a 17-period set against $44.06B for 2025-04-27, not across all periods (Management claims check, Class B release).

One of those statements quotes 'First-quarter revenue was a record $75.2 billion, up 21% from the previous quarter and up 92% from a year ago' while the check compares it against $81.61B reported for 2026-04-26; the material does not reconcile the two figures.

threads.title: R&D intensity
threads.reading: Research and development expense fell to 8.6% of revenues for the year ended 2026-01-25 from 9.9% for the year ended 2025-01-26, a 13.4% move in the ratio against a rule threshold of 8% — the only ratio any check flagged (Class A, 10-K filed 2026-02-25). It sits beside a revenue line the claims check verified as rising sharply. The material reports the ratio but no dollar amounts, so whether the fall came from spending or from the denominator cannot be read off this evidence.
supporting: The ratio move sits against a verified revenue increase: $81.61B for the quarter ended 2026-04-26 versus $44.06B for 2025-04-27 (Management claims check, Class B release matched to Class A figures).
No other condition or ratio check crossed a threshold — financial condition and single-source supply language both came back clear (Class A).
The concept measured is ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense over Revenues, both read from the 10-K filed 2026-02-25 rather than from any outside source (Class A).
against: R&D as a share of revenues moved -13.4%, from 9.9% to 8.6%, crossing the rule's 8% threshold in the direction of less R&D per dollar of revenue (Class A, 10-K filed 2026-02-25).

The check reports only the ratio; with no dollar figures on the page, the fall cannot be attributed to spending or to a rising denominator, so the reassuring reading and the unfavourable one are equally available (same check).

sources.label: 10-K filed 2026-02-25, R&D as a share of revenues

threads.title: New counterparty language against outside reports
threads.reading: Of 24 risk factors the filing added one and removed none: 'Commercial arrangements expose us to counterparty risks.' Sixteen were modified and seven left unchanged, so the section is otherwise stable and the single addition is what changed. Class F items dated 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-22 report a $6B license payment to an AI startup and customer notifications of price increases above 15% — commercial arrangements and pricing that the added factor's subject matter touches but that no Class A source here covers.
supporting: No risk factors were removed and seven of 24 were left unchanged — the addition extends the section rather than swapping anything out (Filing language check, Class A).
The counterparty exposure is disclosed in the filing itself, in the same period as the reported growth (Filing language check, Class A, 10-K filed 2026-02-25).
Nothing in the financial condition or single-source supply language checks crossed a threshold alongside the new language (Class A).
against: The one addition to the entire risk section names counterparty risk arising from commercial arrangements, and no check on this page supplies figures for the size, number or concentration of those arrangements (Filing language check, Class A).

Class F reports dated 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-22 describe a $6B license payment to an AI startup and price increases above 15% notified to customers; these point at commercial and pricing activity the Class A material does not reach, and as Class F they can raise the question but establish nothing (Hacker News mentions, Class F — corroboration only).

sources.label: Bloomberg via Hacker News: customers notified about price hikes above 15%, 2026-08-22
Bloomberg via Hacker News: reported $6B license to an AI startup, 2026-08-20

brief.corroboration: The Class B earnings release is the only non-primary material that could be tested against filed figures; its headline revenue number held up across all 63 reported periods while two of its 'record' framings held only within the same fiscal quarter. The Class F items — press and one developer blog surfaced through Hacker News — point at pricing actions, a large license payment and benchmark results; they can mark a subject for a later filing to answer but cannot establish any of it, and no Class A source here speaks to them.
not_checked: 7 of 10 management claims were not testable against a filed figure (Management claims check).
The two quoted first-quarter revenue figures in the tested material, $81.6 billion and $75.2 billion, are not reconciled anywhere in the material.

The financial condition check reports only that nothing crossed a threshold and supplies no figures, so margins, income and cash position cannot be characterized from this material; the same applies to the single-source supply language check.
Revenue composition was read from the annual segment revenue schedule only; no interim period composition was checked.
The 8-K filed 2026-08-17 reporting entry into a material definitive agreement and creation of a direct financial obligation is listed in the filing feed, but its contents were not part of any check.
The Class F reports of price increases and of a license payment have no Class A counterpart in this material and could not be checked against any filing.
